text:
Ilya Sorokin keeps doing what he did last season, and the Islanders keep needing him to. He has saved 11.1 goals more than his shots usually allow (goals saved above expected), in the 89th percentile among goalies, with a .918 save percentage and an 8-4-2 record in 14 starts. Newsday's headline put the frustration plainly: "Islanders can't keep wasting Ilya Sorokin's great nights in net."

The biggest gains come from the middle of the danger range. He is stopping 90.4% of medium-danger shots against a league 86.3%, worth seven goals on his own, and his low-danger work is clean too. On the hardest chances he is right at league average, which is where most goalies live.

He has been this good for a while. Last season he was +22.3 by our numbers in 55 games, and Evolving-Hockey had him at +52.3. His last five starts are worth +5.2, including 37 saves in a shootout loss in San Jose. Among goalies, he ranks 11th of 77 in wins added by saves this season. When the Islanders win, he is usually the reason.
